start.name: El-Tina area / Sinai-side gas-grid trunk origin near El-Qantara Sharq, opposite Port Said (UNCONFIRMED as this specific line's start -- see notes)
start.coord_basis: Rough proxy only: OSM node 'محطة التينة' (El-Tina railway Station), on the Ismailia road, tagged as Port Said Governorate (not the Sinai/east bank). This is the nearest independently-geocodable place bearing the name 'El-Tina' -- but the EIA source that actually establishes 'El-Tina East' as a Sinai-side gas-trunk origin (for the separate Abr Sinai/El-Tina East-El-Arish pipeline, 111 km) gives no coordinate, only that it sits in the 'El-Tina plain', south of El-Qantara Sharq town (30.8636N 32.3252E) on the Sinai/east-canal-bank side. This node may therefore be the wrong bank entirely.

end.name: Ayoun Moussa Steam Power Station (Suez thermal power station complex near the Ahmed Hamdi Tunnel crossing)
end.coord_basis: OSM landuse=industrial polygon explicitly named 'محطة كهرباء عيون موسى البخارية' / name:en 'Oyoun Mousa Power Station' (way id 210209240) -- a direct, named-facility match, not a settlement proxy.

corridor_desc: GEM's own StartState/EndState 'North Sinia' is directionally consistent with a Sinai-side (east-bank) trunk, but the actual power station polygon (verified via OSM) sits at 29.91N/32.60E near the Ahmed Hamdi Tunnel crossing -- OSM's own reverse-geocode tags that specific spot 'Suez' governorate, and multiple independent tourism/geography sources place the Ayoun Moussa/Ayun Musa toponym in South Sinai (~20-25 km south of the tunnel), not North Sinai. GEM's governorate field for this row may be wrong on both ends (flagged, not corrected). The EIB's 1998 press release for GASCO's financing of 'two gas pipelines, one on each bank of the Suez Canal ... to carry natural gas from Egypt's offshore fields in the Mediterranean Sea to the Ayoun Moussa Power Station in the Sinai' establishes the general feed concept (Mediterranean-sourced gas via a west-bank + Sinai-bank pipeline pair) but describes a 275 km EIB-financed project -- likely a distinct or predecessor project to this 145 km/24in line, not a confirmed match. No source found ties a specific named northern origin point to THIS 145 km pipeline; a WebSearch AI summary that claimed a GASCO trunk 'passing by Oyoun Mousa, El-Arish & Rafah ending in Sharm El-Sheikh' could NOT be confirmed against the archived source text (the actual article at theenergyyear.com only says the grid 'is extending east to Sinai ... and along the coast of the Red Sea', a much vaguer statement) -- that specific claim is discarded as unverifiable, per the hard rule against fabrication.

facts.source: https://egyptoil-gas.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EGAS-Annual-Report-2018-EN.pdf (sheet-cited; this pipeline was NOT found as a distinct line-item in this PDF's FY2017/2018 completed/under-construction tables -- it may be an older line the report only covers in aggregate/historical grid-length figures, not a named table row)

flags: governorate-check: sheet lists North Sinai for both Start/End; independent sources place the Ayoun Moussa toponym in South Sinai or, per OSM's boundary tagging of the power-station polygon itself, in Suez governorate -- worth a second look, not corrected here
seed-source-mismatch: length/diameter cited to EGAS-2018 PDF but not locatable as a named row in that document's grid-pipeline tables
notes: END is solid: an OSM industrial-landuse polygon carries the exact bilingual name match (Arabic 'محطة كهرباء عيون موسى البخارية', name:en 'Oyoun Mousa Power Station'), independently corroborated as a real gas-fired plant in Suez by power-technology.com and PGESCo's own project page (both fetched but gave only city-level location text, not coordinates -- so not cited as route_refs, only as background corroboration of the plant's existence and fuel type). Also corroborated: an OSM-mapped checkpoint 'كمين عيون موسى' (Ayoun Moussa checkpoint) sits 8 km further south on the Sharm El-Sheikh road at 29.8604N/32.6597E, confirming 'Ayoun Moussa' as a real, geographically consistent place-name cluster (not a typo), matching the ~29.87N/32.65E area given in the task brief. START could not be defensibly pinned: EGAS-2018 PDF (the sheet's own cited source) does not contain this pipeline as a named row (grep across the full pdftotext output for 'Ayoun/Moussa/Mousa' returns nothing -- the report's grid-pipeline tables only cover pipelines completed/under construction in FY2017/2018, and this line is evidently older). The EIB 1998 press release confirms the general feed concept (Mediterranean offshore gas via parallel west-bank/Sinai-bank pipelines to Ayoun Moussa) but is for a 275 km project, likely not a 1:1 match to this 145 km/24in line. Recommend leaving RouteAccuracy at 'no route' or, at most, marking only the END point at moderate accuracy pending a named Sinai-side origin.  abarrelfull was not consulted (banned).

end.name: Abu Sultan Power Station (Ismailia Governorate, west of the Great Bitter Lake)
end.coord_basis: Wikidata coordinate for 'Abu Sultan Power Station' (Q56359816), 30°24'7"N 32°18'32"E -- a named, sourced facility entry, not a settlement proxy. This coordinate is essentially IDENTICAL (within ~30 m) to the 'Abu Sultan gas hub' tie-in point already independently derived for sibling PID P8002 (El Tina-Abu Sultan-NAC) from a presidency.eg project registry -- strong cross-corroboration from two unrelated source chains.

corridor_desc: Runs from Ain Sokhna town/port on the Gulf of Suez coast, north-northwest inland roughly parallel to the Ain Sokhna-Cairo highway through New Suez (Suez Governorate), crossing near the Ain Sokhna-Cairo Road / Wadi Hagul Road junction (29.6749N/32.2522E -- an independently-sourced mid-route tie-in chamber for a DIFFERENT, later branch line, P7574, but confirming this trunk's own corridor), continuing northwest to the Abu Sultan gas/power hub west of the Great Bitter Lake near Ismailia.

facts.source: https://egyptoil-gas.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EGAS-Annual-Report-2018-EN.pdf (sheet-cited; not located as a distinct FY2017/2018 table row, same caveat as P8026) -- diameter (32in) independently corroborated by elbalad.news's 2016 Official Gazette report, which names 'the Abu Sultan-Ain Sokhna gas line' explicitly as an existing 32-inch trunk

notes: Well-corroborated, no identity confusion with GEM's existing P8002 'El Tina Abu Sultan New Administrative Capital' segment: P8002 runs El Tina (north, near Port Said) -> Abu Sultan -> New Administrative Capital (further west), i.e. it PASSES THROUGH Abu Sultan from the north, continuing on to NAC. This pipeline (P8033) instead approaches Abu Sultan FROM THE SOUTH, originating at Ain Sokhna. Both are real, distinct, verified segments that converge on the same Abu Sultan hub -- confirmed by a THIRD independent chain: a 2016 elbalad.news article covering an Official Gazette land-appropriation decree for yet another branch (P7574, New Administration Capital PS Gas Pipeline) explicitly describes its start as a 'starting chamber on the Abu Sultan-Ain Sokhna gas line at the intersection of the Ain Sokhna-Cairo road with Wadi Hagul road' -- i.e. it names THIS pipeline (P8033) by corridor and diameter (32in, matching exactly) as an existing trunk that P7574 taps into. A GASCO network-map slide deck (slideshare) independently lists 'Abu Sultan, Ras Bakr, Koraymat' as named facilities on the national grid map, further corroborating Abu Sultan as a real hub. Confidence: high on both endpoints' identity and the corridor; moderate-high on exact coordinates (Abu Sultan is a named facility point; Ain Sokhna is a settlement-level anchor, not the specific tie-in chamber).

end.name: Abu Sultan Power Station (Ismailia Governorate, west of the Great Bitter Lake)
end.coord_basis: Wikidata coordinate for 'Abu Sultan Power Station' (Q56359816) -- same facility/coordinate used for sibling PID P8033's end and independently corroborated for P8002's Abu Sultan hub tie-in.

corridor_desc: Runs east-southeast from Mit Nama, a GASCO grid junction village in Qalyubia just north of Cairo, across the Delta/east-of-Cairo desert to the Abu Sultan hub west of the Great Bitter Lake near Ismailia -- a roughly 114 km cross-country corridor consistent with the sheet's length. Mit Nama is independently confirmed as a real, active gas-grid node (not just a village name) by a separate presidency.eg-registered project, the 'Nubariya-Mit Nama gas line' (Phase 1: 42in/34km, completed Feb 2015; Phase 2: 32in/38km), which feeds the North Giza power station FROM the Nile Delta/Nubariya direction INTO Mit Nama -- i.e. Mit Nama functions as a fan-out point receiving gas from the west and (per this pipeline) sending it east to Abu Sultan.

facts.source: https://egyptoil-gas.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EGAS-Annual-Report-2018-EN.pdf (sheet-cited; not located as a distinct FY2017/2018 table row, same caveat as P8026/P8033)

notes: Moderate-high confidence. Abu Sultan end is a named, sourced facility coordinate reused/cross-checked across three independent chains in this batch (see P8033/P8002 notes). Mit Nama start is a settlement-level anchor (Wikidata village point), not a surveyed station footprint, but is independently corroborated as a genuine, active GASCO grid junction by the separate Nubariya-Mit Nama project reporting (Arabic press: elwatannews.com/algomhor.com articles, fetch blocked by anti-bot 403 so not cited directly as a route_ref; presidency.eg project-registry page for that separate project IS citable and independently confirms the place's role). end.name: Ain Sokhna (town/port area, Suez Governorate)

start.name: Port Said (city/governorate -- UGDC's natural-gas-derivatives extraction plant location)
start.coord_basis: OSM place=city node for Port Said -- settlement-level anchor. UGDC (United Gas Derivatives Company) is independently confirmed by TWO separate sources to have its main NGL/derivatives extraction plant in Port Said: (1) Egypt Energy Monitor's company profile ('UGDC was established to receive gas produced from North Port Said, Ras El Bar and Temsah concessions through the gas treatment plants of El Gamil and Ha'py... operates a natural gas liquids (NGL) facility in Port Said'), and (2) GASCO's own chairman, in a 2024 The Energy Year interview (Wayback-verified), naming 'UGDC's natural gas derivatives extraction plant in Port Said' directly. A more specific address for the plant (Damietta Road KM 12, El Gamil Zone, west of Port Said) surfaced in search results but could NOT be independently re-verified against a live primary source (ugdco.com's own site has since been rebuilt on WordPress and no longer serves the specific old page) -- so the city-level anchor is used instead of the more specific but unconfirmed El Gamil coordinate.
